html:
Meroe was the southern capital of the Kingdom of Kush, on the east bank of the Nile in today's Sudan, north of Khartoum. On the map from 500 BCE to 400 CE its name stands for the whole late kingdom, often called the Meroitic kingdom.

Kush was an old Nubian state. Its kings had once conquered Egypt and ruled it as pharaohs in the 700s BCE. After they lost Egypt, their centre moved south, from Napata to Meroe, which was safer from Egyptian armies and lay in a land of summer rain, with cattle pasture and farmland away from the river.

Meroe was:

  • An iron working centre, with great heaps of slag still around the town.
  • A royal burial ground, with over two hundred steep Nubian pyramids.
  • A meeting point of Egyptian, African and Greek ideas. Its people worshipped Egyptian gods next to their own lion god Apedemak.
  • The home of the Meroitic script, which can be read aloud but whose language is still mostly not understood.

Several ruling queens, called kandakes, are known. One of them, Amanirenas, fought the armies of Augustus after Rome took Egypt, from about 25 to 21 BCE, and the war ended in a treaty on good terms for Kush.

The kingdom weakened in the 200s and 300s CE, as trade moved to the Red Sea and nomads such as the Blemmyes pressed on its lands. Around 350 CE the king of Aksum, Ezana, campaigned in the region, and Meroe fades from the record. Its pyramids are now a World Heritage Site.
sum: Meroe was the southern capital of the Kingdom of Kush, on the east bank of the Nile in today's Sudan, north of Khartoum. On the map from 500 BCE to 400 CE its name stands for the whole late kingdom, often called the Meroitic kingdom.
